## Background

I studied at the University of Toronto before beginning my career in property and casualty (P&C) insurance. Over the next three and a half years, I worked with claims/loss data, quantitative models, and analytical workflows used to evaluate risk and support insurance valuation. This experience gave me a strong foundation in insurance/loss modelling and a better understanding of how analytical results are applied in supporting better decisions in handling risk and uncertainty.

## Why Data Science

Working with data and loss models made me increasingly interested in methods beyond the traditional actuarial approaches I had been using. In particular, I became interested in machine learning, AI, and how stronger programming and automation can improve analytical actuarial works. I joined UBC’s Master of Data Science program to develop these capabilities more systematically, from statistical and machine-learning methods to programming, data workflows, and collaborative software development.

## What I Want to Build

I am particularly interested in moving beyond simply using AI tools toward building reliable AI-enabled analytical workflows. I want to strengthen my ability to develop and validate modelling pipelines, automate repetitive analytical processes, and apply stronger software-engineering practices through my data science training. Over time, I hope to combine these skills with my industry experience to build tools and models that are technically sound and useful in practice.
